title: Getting started with rmoriedata
text: Release counts, means, histograms calibrated noise. Smaller epsilon means stronger privacy noise.
code: set.seed(1)  # A private count of records matching a predicate. morie_dp_laplace_count(true_count = 42, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 41.36704  # The mechanism is unbiased -- averaging many releases recovers the truth. mean(replicate(2000, morie_dp_laplace_count(42, epsilon = 1.0))) #> [1] 41.98688  # A private mean of bounded data. x <- runif(1000, 0, 1) morie_dp_gaussian_mean(x, lower = 0, upper = 1, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 0.4893552  # A private histogram straight from tabulated data. counts <- as.integer(table(comp$year)) round(pmax(0, morie_dp_laplace_histogram(counts, epsilon = 1.0))) #> [1] 24999     2

title: Getting started with rmoriedata
text: Check release standard disclosure-control thresholds publishing . Cell suppression hides small counts (default) applies complementary suppression hidden values can’t recovered marginals:
code: df <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 25, 25, 32, 32, 40),   sex = c("F", "F", "F", "M", "M", "M") )  # k-anonymity: every quasi-identifier combo must appear >= k times. morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), k = 2)$summary #> [1] "k=2: VIOLATED (min class size=1; 1/3 classes below threshold)"  # l-diversity: each class must hold >= l distinct sensitive values. df2 <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 25, 25, 25, 32, 32, 32),   sex = c("F", "F", "F", "F", "M", "M", "M"),   dx  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "X", "Y", "Z") ) morie_l_diversity_verify(df2, c("age", "sex"), "dx", l = 3)$summary #> [1] "l=3: SATISFIED (min diversity=3; 0/2 classes below threshold)" tbl <- matrix(c(120, 3, 47, 88, 2, 99, 14, 51, 60), nrow = 3,               dimnames = list(c("A", "B", "C"), c("X", "Y", "Z"))) res <- morie_cell_suppress(tbl, threshold = 5) res$suppressed #>     X  Y  Z #> A 120 NA 14 #> B  NA NA NA #> C  NA 99 60

what: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
text: Releases approximately (\(\epsilon\), \(\delta\))-DP mean bounded numeric vector. Sensitivity derived user-asserted bounds: changing one record can shift sum upper - lower, mean's sensitivity (upper - lower) / length(x).

title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
code: morie_dp_gaussian_mean(x, lower, upper, epsilon, delta = 1e-06)

title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
text: x Numeric vector (NAs). lower, upper Hard bounds `x`. Caller must guarantee (x >= lower & x <= upper); function clips defensively emits warning clipping necessary. epsilon, delta Privacy parameters. Standard recommendation: delta < 1/length(x), epsilon 0.1 5.0.

title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
text: noised mean (single numeric).

title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
text: noise standard deviation follows classical analytic-Gaussian calibration: $$\sigma = \frac{\Delta \cdot \sqrt{2 \ln(1.25/\delta)}}{\epsilon}.$$

title: Differentially-private mean via the Gaussian mechanism with bounded inputs — morie_dp_gaussian_mean
code: set.seed(1) x <- runif(1000, 0, 1)  # A private mean of bounded data (bounds asserted by the caller). morie_dp_gaussian_mean(x, lower = 0, upper = 1, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 0.5001013 mean(x)                                  # the true mean, for comparison #> [1] 0.4996917  # `delta` controls the (epsilon, delta) guarantee; smaller = stronger. morie_dp_gaussian_mean(x, 0, 1, epsilon = 1.0, delta = 1e-9) #> [1] 0.4977702  # Wider bounds raise sensitivity, so the same epsilon adds more noise. morie_dp_gaussian_mean(x, lower = -5, upper = 5, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 0.436994  # Out-of-range values are clipped to [lower, upper] (with a warning). y <- c(x, 2, -1) suppressWarnings(morie_dp_gaussian_mean(y, lower = 0, upper = 1, epsilon = 1)) #> [1] 0.499752

what: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
text: Adds Laplace noise calibrated sensitivity / epsilon. Use releasing counts records matching predicate (e.g. number UoF incidents division-year). Sensitivity hardcoded 1: one record entering leaving dataset changes count 1.

title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
code: morie_dp_laplace_count(true_count, epsilon)

title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
text: true_count Non-negative integer; true count. epsilon Privacy budget (smaller = noise = stronger privacy). Typical range: 0.1 5.0.

title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
text: noised count (numeric, may fractional negative). Caller   usually clip non-negative integer display:   round(pmax(0, x)).

title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
text: Pure (\(\epsilon\), 0)-differentially-private standard add--remove-one neighbouring-databases definition.

title: Differentially-private count via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_count
code: set.seed(1) # A single noised release of a true count of 42. morie_dp_laplace_count(true_count = 42, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 41.36704  # Smaller epsilon = stronger privacy = more noise. morie_dp_laplace_count(42, epsilon = 0.1)   # noisier #> [1] 39.04619 morie_dp_laplace_count(42, epsilon = 5.0)   # closer to 42 #> [1] 42.0315  # The mechanism is unbiased: averaging many releases returns ~the truth. mean(replicate(2000, morie_dp_laplace_count(42, epsilon = 1.0))) #> [1] 41.98897  # For display, clip to a non-negative integer. round(pmax(0, morie_dp_laplace_count(3, epsilon = 0.5))) #> [1] 3

what: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
title: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
text: Adds independent Laplace(1/epsilon) noise bin count. add--remove-one neighbouring-databases definition single record participates exactly one bin, per-bin sensitivity 1 overall mechanism (\(\epsilon\), 0)-DP.

title: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
code: morie_dp_laplace_histogram(counts, epsilon)

title: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
text: counts Integer vector non-negative bin counts. epsilon Privacy budget (positive scalar).

title: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
text: numeric vector length `counts`. May contain   fractional negative values. Caller responsible post-hoc   non-negativity / rounding display.

title: Differentially-private histogram via the Laplace mechanism — morie_dp_laplace_histogram
code: set.seed(1) true <- c(120, 45, 8, 230, 17)  # Independent Laplace noise added to every bin. morie_dp_laplace_histogram(true, epsilon = 0.5) #> [1] 118.734079  44.409238   8.314961 233.390161  15.184168  # Smaller epsilon = more noise per bin. morie_dp_laplace_histogram(true, epsilon = 0.1) #> [1] 135.934630  67.013881  11.880117 232.987135  -3.909269  # Post-process for display: clip negatives, round to integers. noisy <- morie_dp_laplace_histogram(true, epsilon = 1.0) round(pmax(0, noisy)) #> [1] 119  44   8 230  18  # Release a private histogram straight from tabulated data. counts <- as.integer(table(complaint_sample$year)) morie_dp_laplace_histogram(counts, epsilon = 1.0) #> [1] 24998.995388     1.571349

title: k-anonymity verification — morie_k_anonymity_verify
text: Checks whether data.frame satisfies k-anonymity supplied quasi-identifier columns. dataset k-anonymous every combination quasi-identifier values appears least `k` rows.

title: k-anonymity verification — morie_k_anonymity_verify
code: morie_k_anonymity_verify(data, quasi_identifiers, k = 5)

title: k-anonymity verification — morie_k_anonymity_verify
text: data data.frame. quasi_identifiers Character vector column names. k Minimum equivalence-class size. Default 5 (common public-health / open-data threshold).

title: k-anonymity verification — morie_k_anonymity_verify
text: list class "morie_k_anon" containing: satisfies logical, whether dataset k-anonymous. k threshold used. min_class_size integer, size smallest class. n_classes integer, total number equivalence classes. n_violations integer, number classes threshold. violating_classes data.frame class keys plus     .n sizes (empty data.frame none). summary human-readable one-line summary.

title: k-anonymity verification — morie_k_anonymity_verify
code: df <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 25, 25, 32, 32, 40),   sex = c("F", "F", "F", "M", "M", "M") )  # k = 2: the class {age=40, sex=M} has only 1 row -> VIOLATED. res <- morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), k = 2) res$summary #> [1] "k=2: VIOLATED (min class size=1; 1/3 classes below threshold)" res$satisfies #> [1] FALSE res$violating_classes        # the offending quasi-identifier combos #>   age sex .n #> 1  40   M  1  # Loosening to k = 1 always holds; the default k = 5 is stricter. morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), k = 1)$satisfies #> [1] TRUE morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"))$satisfies   # k = 5 #> [1] FALSE  # A single quasi-identifier is fine too. morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, "sex", k = 3)$min_class_size #> [1] 3  # On real bundled data: are (year, arrest) cells 5-anonymous? morie_k_anonymity_verify(complaint_sample,   c("year", "arrest"), k = 5)$summary #> [1] "k=5: VIOLATED (min class size=1; 1/3 classes below threshold)"

title: l-diversity verification — morie_l_diversity_verify
text: Checks whether data.frame satisfies l-diversity: within equivalence class defined quasi-identifiers, sensitive attribute must take least `l` distinct values.

title: l-diversity verification — morie_l_diversity_verify
code: morie_l_diversity_verify(data, quasi_identifiers, sensitive, l = 3)

title: l-diversity verification — morie_l_diversity_verify
text: data data.frame. quasi_identifiers Character vector QI column names. sensitive Name sensitive-attribute column. l Minimum number distinct sensitive values per class. Default 3.

title: l-diversity verification — morie_l_diversity_verify
text: list class "morie_l_div" containing: satisfies logical. l threshold used. min_diversity integer, lowest per-class distinct count. n_classes integer. n_violations integer, classes threshold. violating_classes data.frame class keys plus     .diversity count. summary human-readable.

title: l-diversity verification — morie_l_diversity_verify
code: df <- data.frame(   age = c(25, 25, 25, 25, 32, 32, 32),   sex = c("F", "F", "F", "F", "M", "M", "M"),   dx  = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "X", "Y", "Z") )  # Class {25,F} has 3 distinct dx (A,B,C); {32,M} has 3 (X,Y,Z) -> l=3 holds. res <- morie_l_diversity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), "dx", l = 3) res$summary #> [1] "l=3: SATISFIED (min diversity=3; 0/2 classes below threshold)" res$satisfies #> [1] TRUE res$min_diversity #> [1] 3  # Demanding l = 4 fails: no class has 4 distinct sensitive values. bad <- morie_l_diversity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), "dx", l = 4) bad$satisfies #> [1] FALSE bad$violating_classes #>   age sex .diversity #> 1  25   F          3 #> 2  32   M          3  # k-anonymity and l-diversity are complementary: check both. morie_k_anonymity_verify(df, c("age", "sex"), k = 3)$satisfies #> [1] TRUE
